newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak EconMin says trade gap a priority - agency.
newsitem.headline: Slovak EconMin says trade gap a priority - agency.

text.p: Slovak Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said curbing the country's widening trade deficit was one of the main economic priorities for 1997, the official TASR agency reported on Friday.

"We can achieve this (curbing the trade deficit) by increasing the dynamism of growth of exports to at least eight percent and by reducing the growth of imports to a maximum 12 percent," TASR qouted Cesnek as saying.

Slovakia posted a 1996 trade deficit of 64.54 billion crowns, up from a 5.69 billion shortfall in 1995, with exports totalling 270.63 billion crowns and imports accounting for 335.17 billion, up 6.1 percent and 28.5 percent, respectively.
The foreign trade gap was at the heart of the country's current account deficit of 59.9 billion crowns, or some 10 percent of the expected 1996 GDP figure.
Cesnek did not elaborate on how the government would slow import growth or boost exports.

He said the main reasons for the rapid growth of imports last year were equipment needs for building the Mochovce nuclear power station, energy imports and equipment necessary for industrial restructuring.
Cesnek also said curbing the trade deficit should not be achieved only through strict monetary policy reducing the money supply growth and thus cutting the ineffective imports.

"We should use mainly a pro-export policy, through the newly-created State Fund to Support Exports and the Eximbank, rather than only the restrictive monetary policy in fighting the trade deficit problem," Cesnek said.

Slovakia's foreign trade balance more than trebled to 7.061 billion crowns in January 1997 year-on-year, from 2.125 billion a year ago, on increased imports of fossil fuels, nuclear plant technology and cars.

Government officials have said the negative development of the trade balance was typical for an economy in transition to a free market and repeatedly rejected calls for a devaluation of the crown to help exports.
